decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted shall be commenced before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.
The materials to be used in the construction of the external surfaces of the development hereby permitted shall match those used in the existing dwellinghouse.

<p><span style="font-size:11pt"><span style="font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Notwithstanding the provisions of The Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (or any order revoking and re-enacting that Order with or without modification), no development falling within CLASS A, B, C, D and E in Part 1 of Schedule 2 to that Order shall be carried out without the prior written permission of the Local Planning Authority. </span></span></p><p style="text-align:justify"><br></p>

<p>A detailed Acoustic Report 
prepared by a competent Acoustic Consultant shall be submitted and approved in writing by 
the Local Planning Authority (LPA). 
 
              The report shall detail all external noise sources that may impact on the future occupiers. The 
report shall include the assessment of noise levels at times representative  
              of the operational hours of nearby transport routes and any commercial operations. 
 
               Where mitigation measures are required to ensure that internal noise levels comply with 
relevant guidance in BS 8233:2014 the report shall detail the required acoustic  
               specification to ensure that an adequate level of sound attenuation is provided.&nbsp;</p>

<p><span style="font-size:11pt">Prior to commencement of the development, a CLP in line with the TfL guidelines shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall include the numbers, size and routes of construction vehicles, provisions within/around the site to ensure that all vehicles associated with the construction works are properly managed to prevent any unwanted disruption to other highway users, and other matters relating to traffic management to be agreed with the licencing officers of the council. Approved details shall be implemented throughout the project period and any changes to the document must be reported back to the council’s planning and highways department.&nbsp;&nbsp;</span></p><p><br></p>

<p><span style="font-size:11pt"><span style="font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The proposed development shall achieve Secured by Design principles to the satisfaction of the Local Planning Authority and the Metropolitan Police, details of which shall be provided to the Local Planning Authority for its written approval prior to the first occupation of the approved development. All security measures applied to the approved development shall be permanently retained thereafter.&nbsp;</span></span></p><p style="text-align:justify"><br></p>

The development hereby approved shall only be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and documents:

- DRAWING XXX REV XX DATED XX
- USE [SHIFT]+[ENTER] FOR REGULAR LINE SPACING
- USE [ENTER] FOR LARGER LINE SPACING

No other drawings or documents apply.

<p><span style="font-size:11pt"><span style="font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">&nbsp;Prior to first occupation, details of the cycle parking facilities, as approved, &nbsp;shall be implemented. The development shall not be occupied until the approved details have been implemented. Thereafter, the cycle parking facilities shall be permanently retained. </span></span></p><p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-size:11pt"><span style="font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif"><em>Reason: In order to promote sustainable forms of transport.</em></span></span></p>

<p><span style="font-size:11pt">Notwithstanding the details submitted with the application, prior to above ground works, full details of waste management shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Prior to occupation, the approved details shall be fully implemented. Thereafter, the refuse storage shall be permanently retained.</span></p><p><br></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-size:11pt">No development shall commence, including any works of demolition, until a Construction Environmental Management Plan (CEMP) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. This Plan shall incorporate details of:</span></p><p><span style="font-size:11pt">a) the parking of site operatives’ vehicles;<br>b) loading and unloading of plant and materials;<br>c) storage of plant and materials used in constructing the development;<br>d) measures to control the emission of dust, dirt, and emissions to air during construction;<br>e) noise and vibration control; and<br>f) a waste management plan for recycling/disposing of waste resulting from demolition and construction works</span></p><p><span style="font-size:11pt">Demolition and construction work and associated activities, other than internal works inaudible outside the site boundary, are only to be carried out between the hours of 08:00 and 18:00 Monday to Friday and 08:00 and 13:00 Saturday, with no work on Sundays or public holidays without the prior written permission of the Local Planning Authority.</span></p><p><span style="font-size:11pt">Any works which are associated with the generation of ground borne vibration are only to be carried out between the hours of 08:00 and 18:00 Monday to Friday.</span></p><p><span style="font-size:11pt">Demolition and construction work and associated activities are to be carried out in accordance with the recommendations contained within British Standard 5228:2009, “Code of practice for noise and vibration control on construction and open sites”, Parts 1 and 2.</span></p><p><span style="font-size:11pt">Once approved the Plan shall be adhered to throughout the construction period for the development.</span></p>

<p>The development hereby permitted shall not be commenced until the following documents (in consultation with 
London Underground), for each progressive stage of the development have been submitted to and approved in 
writing by the local planning authority which: 
1. provide detailed design and Risk Assessment Method Statement on the use of tall plant, cranes, scaffolding 
and lifting equipment, if any 
2. before work commences on site, an assessment of railway noise and vibration shall be carried out and 
appropriate protective measures shall be taken, to protect the users of the property and of other properties 
potentially affected, against noise and vibration, as a result of the current development.&nbsp;</p>

<div style="font-family: &quot;Segoe UI&quot;; line-height: 20px;"><p>Prior to first occupation of the development hereby approved, a scheme shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, in consultation with the Highway Authority, detailing measures to prevent the parking of vehicles on the adjacent highway verge and to ensure that the access hereby approved is used for pedestrian purposes only. The approved scheme may include, but is not limited to, physical measures such as boundary treatments, bollards, landscaping, or other appropriate deterrents and shall be implemented in full prior to first use of the development and retained thereafter for the lifetime of the development.</p><p>The approved access shall be used for pedestrian access only and shall not be used to facilitate vehicular access, parking, loading, unloading, or the crossing of the highway verge by vehicles at any time</p></div>

<p><span style="font-size:11pt">The effect of paragraph 13 of Schedule 7A to the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 is that planning permission granted for the development of land in England is deemed to have been granted subject to the condition “(the biodiversity gain condition”) that <strong>development may not begin unless:</strong></span></p><p><span style="font-size:11pt"><strong>(a) a Biodiversity Gain Plan has been submitted to the planning authority, and</strong></span></p><p><span style="font-size:11pt"><strong>(b) the planning authority has approved the plan.</strong></span></p><p><span style="font-size:11pt">The planning authority, for the purposes of determining whether to approve a Biodiversity Gain Plan in respect of this permission would be London Borough of Barking and Dagenham.</span></p><p><span style="font-size:11pt">Based on the information available this permission is considered to be one which will require the approval of a biodiversity gain plan before development is begun because none of the statutory exemptions or transitional arrangements are considered to apply.</span></p><p><span style="font-size:11pt">Please see informatives and notes for further information in relation to the condition, exemptions, transitional arrangements, irreplaceable habitats and the effect of 73(D) of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.</span></p>

<p>The building envelope of the development to which the application refers shall be constructed 
to provide sound attenuation against externally generated noise sources to achieve the 
internal ambient noise levels detailed in Table 1 below.  
 
               The measured or calculated noise levels shall be determined in accordance with the latest 
British Standard 8233:2014 “Guidance on sound insulation and noise  
                reduction for buildings” .  
                
                Details of the scheme shall be in accordance with the specification given in the approved 
Noise Impact Assessment and shall be submitted to the Local Planning  
                Authority (LPA) for approval in writing.  Any works which form part of the scheme shall be 
completed in accordance with the approved details before the dwellings  
                are occupied and shall thereafter be retained as approved. 
 
2
                 Internal noise levels should be achieved with windows open for rapid ventilation purposes. 
Where this cannot be achieved alternative means of ventilation and cooling  
                 will be required. Where whole house ventilation is provided then acoustically treated inlets 
and outlets should ideally be located away from the façade(s) most exposed  
                 to noise (and any local sources of air pollution). Any ventilation strategy shall consider the 
Association of Noise Consultants ‘Acoustics, Ventilation and Overheating:  
                 Residential Design Guide’ (2020).&nbsp;&nbsp; The design and layout of the development shall be constructed so as to protect external 
amenity spaces (including gardens, balconies and terraces) against externally  
               Generated noise sources to achieve 50dB(A) LAeq,16hour with a maximum limit of 55dB(A) 
LAeq,16hour. Any works which form part of the scheme shall be completed in  
               accordance with the approved details before the dwellings are occupied and shall thereafter 
be retained as approved. The measured or calculated noise levels shall be  
               determined in accordance with the Professional Practice Guidance: Planning &amp; Noise – New 
Residential Development’ (2017). </p>
description: Construction of a new two- storey 4x bed dwelling including a dormer window to the front, with associated external amenity area, hard and soft landscaping and cycle and refuse storage at land to the rear of 144 Reede Road Dagenham RM10 8DX
borough: London Borough of Barking and Dagenham
